newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos says ASEAN to discuss Burma membership.
newsitem.headline: Ramos says ASEAN to discuss Burma membership.

text.p: This week's ASEAN summit will definitely discuss the question of Burma's entry to the Southeast Asian grouping, Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday.

"Yes, definitely ... We will continue looking at ASEAN plus three," Ramos told reporters when asked if the informal seven-nation summit in Jakarta on Saturday would take up the question of membership of Burma, Laos and Cambodia.
Ramos said the consensus of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations was that the three candidates "must go through the step-by-step process" of membership.

He said that "maybe the most basic of the steps" was for each new member to see if they could conform to the ASEAN goal of lowering tariffs "so that a really free and open kind of inter-ASEAN market can really ensue".

ASEAN, which comprises the Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore, Brunei and Vietnam, is seeking to create a free trade area where tariffs on a group of products would be cut to 0-5 percent by 2003.
The Burma issue has dominated ASEAN since the military government in Rangoon launched a fresh crackdown on the democracy movement of Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi in April.
Western nations and human rights activists have said that accepting Burma's application for full membership in ASEAN would be tantamount to approving Rangoon's policies.
ASEAN follows a policy of not interfering in members' internal affairs and maintains that constructive engagement with Burma is the best way to achieve political reform in that country.
